questions.q: Name the first oil-producing region in India before the establishment of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission in 1956.
questions.a: Digboi in Assam was the only oil-producing region before 1956. A wrong answer (e.g., Mumbai High or Ankaleshwar) reveals the student does not know the historical sequence of oil exploration in India and confuses pre- and post-ONGC discoveries.

questions.q: Why are petroleum reserves in India confined to sedimentary basins of the tertiary period?
questions.a: Petroleum forms from organic matter buried in sedimentary basins; tertiary period basins (like Assam, Gujarat, Mumbai offshore) provided the right conditions of source rock, reservoir rock, and structural traps. A wrong answer (e.g., "because of volcanic activity" or "found in igneous rocks") shows the student misunderstands the geological origin of petroleum and confuses it with mineral deposits associated with igneous/metamorphic rocks.

questions.q: On an outline map of India, mark and label the following: (a) Mumbai High, (b) Ankaleshwar, (c) Digboi, (d) Krishna-Godavari basin. Then state which of these is an offshore field.
questions.a: (a) Mumbai High — 160 km west of Mumbai in Arabian Sea (offshore); (b) Ankaleshwar — Gujarat (onshore); (c) Digboi — Assam (onshore); (d) Krishna-Godavari basin — east coast (offshore/onshore). Mumbai High and Krishna-Godavari basin are offshore. A wrong location (e.g., placing Mumbai High on land) reveals poor map skills and confusion between onshore and offshore fields.

questions.q: Compare the distribution of petroleum and natural gas reserves in India. What pattern do you observe, and what geological reason explains it?
questions.a: Both petroleum and natural gas occur in the same sedimentary basins (Assam, Gujarat, Mumbai High, Krishna-Godavari, Kaveri) because natural gas is often associated with petroleum deposits, released when crude oil is brought to the surface. A wrong answer that separates their distributions (e.g., "natural gas only in Rajasthan") indicates the student missed the genetic link between the two resources.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Field-based refineries are more economical than market-based refineries for India's petroleum industry." Use examples from the text.
questions.a: Field-based refineries (e.g., Digboi) process crude oil near the source, reducing transport cost of crude, but market-based refineries (e.g., Barauni) are located near consumption centres, reducing product transport cost. The optimum depends on pipeline infrastructure and demand patterns. A one-sided answer ignoring the trade-off shows lack of evaluative geographical reasoning.

questions.q: Design a one-page annotated map for a Class 12 geography project showing India's petroleum and natural gas pipeline network (GAIL's 'One Nation One Grid'), major refineries, and consumption centres. List the key elements you would include.
questions.a: A good answer includes: (1) outline map of India with sedimentary basins shaded, (2) symbols for oil fields (onshore/offshore), gas fields, (3) pipeline routes (existing and proposed) with GAIL network, (4) refinery locations labelled as field-based or market-based, (5) major consumption centres (metros, industrial clusters), (6) legend, scale, and north arrow. A poor answer misses the pipeline network or fails to distinguish refinery types, showing incomplete synthesis.
